brief.ask: Set the art direction for 12 boys' birthday evites (dinosaurs, space, trucks, soccer, pirates, heroes, robots, sharks, safari, knights, race cars, ninjas). Each one has a 15-second tap game or scratch-and-reveal before the details. Say what makes a parent forward this instead of a text.
brief.audience: Parents of 3 to 10 year olds sending to other parents; the kids play the game on a parent's phone.
brief.feeling: Wonder and momentum, a toy brought to life, never cheap or loud for its own sake.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
references: Exploration grid A: collectible-toy 3D dinosaurs in a golden-hour jungle with a glowing volcano and balloons; warm, film-grade; empty dirt foreground for type.
Exploration grid B: painterly nebula space scenes, a small rocket past a ringed planet and a smiling moon; deep blue starfield bottom third for type.

proposals.title: Twelve Measures, One Occasion
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single governed composition — a cantus firmus of one strong structural axis, one earned focal light, and one moment of formal resolution — so that the 15-second game is not a distraction bolted on but the downbeat from which the invitation's full form is revealed.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390×844px canvas divided by a single golden-section horizontal at 61% of height; above the line is the full-bleed art plate, below is a type field whose proportions echo the upper plate's dominant internal rectangle. The game or scratch zone occupies the exact golden-section rectangle centered in the art plate — not arbitrary, not full-bleed, but a framed stage within the image, the way a choir-loft arch frames the performance. All twelve themes share this armature; what varies is the dominant axis within it: diagonal for Pirates and Ninjas, radial for Space and Robots, vertical for Knights and Heroes, low-horizon for Trucks and Race Cars, foliage-depth for Safari and Dinosaurs, surge-wave for Sharks and Soccer.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Playfair Display (OFL, Google Fonts) — used at large scale, tight tracking, mixed case, anchored to the baseline of the type field. Secondary and detail: DM Sans (OFL, Google Fonts) — set at 13–15px, generous leading, sentence case, never competing with the display line. Theme name as a single display word printed at ~72px, weight Regular, no outline, no drop shadow — its legibility depends on the contrast architecture of the plate beneath it, which is the structural commitment. Date, venue, RSVP in DM Sans at a fixed small scale, left-aligned to the golden-section left margin. No decorative type treatments; the image earns the drama, the type holds the measure.
proposals.imageLogic: All plates generated via Magnific draft grid, one prompt per thematic cluster. Prompt discipline: every plate is directed to carry a single motivated light source at a consistent upper-left or upper-right position across the collection — this is the cantus firmus of the image grammar, the rule that lets WebGL foil highlights lock to the same vector on every theme without visual contradiction. Plates are composed with a clean lower third (dark ground, mist, water, shadow, soil — theme-appropriate) so live type is never placed over narrative detail. Foreground cut-out layers (the drifting tilt-reactive elements) are generated separately against transparency: a T-rex mid-stride, a rocket exhaust plume, a knight's raised visor, a shark fin — each extracted as a Magnific asset with simulated subsurface or reflective material. No photographic stock. No scan. The 8–16-plate grid per prompt mean
proposals.texture: Simulated film grain at 12% opacity overlaid as a procedural noise shader — not decorative, but a unifying membrane that prevents the generative plates from reading as CGI-smooth. The scratch-and-reveal game surface uses a simulated silver foil layer (WebGL shader, physically-plausible anisotropic highlight) that the child's drag gesture removes in strips, exposing the art plate beneath — the reveal is structurally satisfying because the foil conceals the composition's focal point, and clearing it completes the picture rather than merely uncovering a prize. The tilt-reactive foreground cut-outs carry a thin specular rim on the side facing the single motivated light source, enforced by the same WebGL light vector — coherence across substrate, as I have noted in my recent working notes.
proposals.motion: Order of events, timed to 15 seconds: 0–0.4s — plate fades in at full opacity, foil layer covers the focal rectangle, ambient particle system begins (theme-specific: spores for Dinosaurs, stars for Space, sparks for Robots, bubbles for Sharks); 0.4–12s — child drags or taps to scratch foil; foreground cut-outs drift on phone tilt at 0.6× gyroscope sensitivity with a 200ms ease-out, never faster than the eye can read them as objects rather than smears; 12–13.5s — foil fully cleared, a single motivated light bloom pulses once from the source position (not a loop, a cadence — one beat, resolved); 13.5–15s — type field rises from 0 to full opacity on a 300ms ease, DM Sans details staggering in at 80ms intervals. After 15s: static. No ambient loop. The invitation does not perform continuously; it resolves, and then it holds.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific draft-grid prompts: Prompt A covers Dinosaurs, Safari, Pirates, Ninjas, Knights (organic, textured, practical-light environments); Prompt B covers Space, Robots, Heroes, Trucks, Race Cars, Soccer, Sharks (hard light, reflective surfaces, constructed or atmospheric environments). Each prompt requests 12–16 plates at the 390×844px ratio with the lower-third clear zone specified in the prompt. Art director selects one plate per theme from the returned grid. Foreground cut-outs generated as a separate Magnific pass per theme, prompted against a neutral ground for clean extraction. WebGL foil, grain, particle, and light-bloom shaders are written once as a parameterized system and skinned per theme by adjusting: particle shape, particle color, foil hue (silver for Knights and Robots, warm gold for Pirates and Dinosaurs, deep violet for Space, matte olive for Safari). Tela document
proposals.humanTrace: The art director's hand is present in three acts: the compositional selection from the draft grid (choosing the plate whose internal geometry best resolves against the golden-section armature, not the most visually busy one); the prompt constraint that enforces the single motivated light source across all twelve themes (a structural decision, not a stylistic one); and the timing sequence of the motion (the single resolved bloom at second 13, the staggered type reveal — these are conducted, not generated). The film grain shader and the foil anisotropy are parameters set by judgment, not defaults.
proposals.risk: The single governed light source and the restrained motion arc may read as austere to parents who expect maximum spectacle for a child's birthday — the Baroque Dramatist will say the reveal does not announce itself loudly enough, and seven-year-olds will not care about golden sections. The risk is worth carrying because restraint is what makes a parent forward this: the evite reads as something made with care, not manufactured noise, and that legibility survives the link-preview thumbnail, the QR print, and the second viewing. A composition that resolves can be remembered. A composition that performs continuously cannot.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the foil reveal to crescendo — a particle burst, a sound cue, a secondary animation that underlines the moment. I will refuse this on structural grounds: a reveal that announces itself is a reveal that does not trust its own content. The composition's focal point, when uncovered, should be sufficient. proposals.title: Torn Open, Still Burning
proposals.idea: Every invite is a contraband zine from inside the world of the theme — ink-bled, edge-torn, pressure-printed — so the parent forwards it because it looks like something they'd want to keep, not delete.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 phone card. The art plate is divided by a brutal diagonal tear roughly at the 60% mark — top zone is the world (jungle, space, ocean floor), bottom zone is a raw kraft-paper band where live type sits. The tear edge is ragged and procedurally unique per theme, never a clean line. Foreground cut-outs float above the tear, half in each zone. The 15-second game lives inside the top zone: a scratch-reveal implemented as a fragment shader that simulates a thick ink overprint being physically scratched away by the child's finger, exposing the party details beneath — the scratch path accumulates and is never undoable, so the card arrives already partially scratched by whoever played it last, carrying evidence of a previous kid's hand.
proposals.typography: Bebas Neue (OFL, Google Fonts) for the theme title — wide, compressed, uppercase, 72–80px, letterspacing 0.05em, set in the kraft band. Literata (OFL, Google Fonts) for names, date, venue at 16–18px regular, generous line-height 1.6 for legibility at 390px. The theme word is knocked out of a block of simulated ink so the kraft shows through the letterform — not a drop shadow, a relief. No gradients on type. Type is never baked.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative plates. Directing two master prompt grids of 12 plates each: Grid C — 'vintage offset-print naturalist field guides rephotographed with raking light, ink halftone dots visible, subject fills 80% of frame, deliberate misregistration in cyan channel, one color slightly out of alignment, warm paper stock, no white backgrounds' — yields dinosaurs, sharks, safari animals, knights, pirates. Grid D — 'Soviet-era science propaganda poster aesthetic, bold flat forms with visible screen-print texture, slight ink bleed at edges, subjects: robots, rockets, race cars, soccer, ninjas, heroes' — yields the mechanical and heroic themes. Both grids use physically plausible single-source raking light from upper-left so the WebGL foil layer has a committed sun position to clamp to. The foreground cut-outs are isolated from the same plates via Magnific's alpha-channel pass.
proposals.texture: The overprint ink layer is a fragment shader simulating letterpress impression: slight deboss shadow on downstroke edges, ink spread heavier in corners than center of letterforms. The kraft band is procedural paper-tooth noise (Perlin + Worley composite) with visible fiber direction running horizontally. The scratch-reveal game uses a canvas mask that accumulates finger paths as rough, slightly-dragged strokes — not clean circles — so the revealed layer beneath has the look of something uncovered rather than unlocked. The WebGL foil shimmer is locked to the misregistration channel of the art plate: it only activates where the cyan ink is out of register, meaning the shimmer is earned by the physical decision baked into the Magnific prompt.
proposals.motion: On load: the art plate drops in as if printed — a 0.3s impression thud with a micro-bounce, no fade. The foreground cut-out (a single hero object per theme — T-rex, rocket, truck) drifts on gyroscope tilt at 4px max parallax, slow and weighted like a physical card being tilted. The kraft band slides up 8px on load then settles — one motion, done. The scratch game: finger contact triggers the shader mask to accumulate; a grain of procedural audio-haptic feedback is recommended but reduced-motion respects the setting and substitutes a tap-count progress bar instead. After reveal: confetti particles burst from the scratch zone — 40 particles max, physics-based, gravity pulls them off screen in 1.2s, no loop. Nothing pulses. Nothing breathes. The card is still once played.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids (C and D above) returning 8–16 plates each at one flat cost, editorial selection of the 12 strongest, alpha-channel isolation pass for foreground cut-outs. Fragment shaders written in GLSL for the scratch-reveal mask, the letterpress impression texture, and the paper-tooth kraft band — all procedural, no scanned assets. The foil shimmer WebGL layer is a pre-built Tela effect clamped to the misregistration mask extracted from the Magnific plate. Bebas Neue and Literata loaded via Google Fonts. Live text fields in Tela for name, date, venue. Reduced-motion variant substitutes the scratch shader with a tap-counter progress bar and static reveal. Total generative cost: two Magnific grid runs.
proposals.humanTrace: The misregistration in the Magnific prompt is a directed decision — I told the model which channel drifts and by how much. The scratch path on each forwarded card is a literal record of the previous child's finger pressure and speed, accumulated in the canvas mask and never reset. The tear geometry at the 60% break is procedurally unique per theme but uses the same seed class, so all 12 feel like they came from the same hand. The raking light angle in the prompt is committed: upper-left, always, so the foil has one sun to answer to.
proposals.risk: The accumulated scratch path means every forwarded card arrives partially revealed — some parents will think it is broken. That is the risk and it is worth it because a card that shows evidence of another child's play is not a template, it is an object with a history, and that is what makes a parent forward it instead of sending a text. The misregistration aesthetic risks reading as low-quality on first glance. Worth it: it reads as intentional within two seconds, and intentional imperfection at consumer-facing resolution is the signal of a maker, not a budget cut.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will strip the kraft band, kill the misregistration, and leave a clean reveal on a white ground — arguing that the scratch mechanic is enough and the texture is noise. I say the texture is not decoration, it is the argument: a clean white card with a scratch game is a feature; a kraft-and-misregistration card with a scratch game is a thing. proposals.title: State Machines Wearing Costumes
proposals.idea: Each evite is a physically-simulated instrument — not a decorated card — where the theme governs the physics rule, the game IS the physics, and the reveal is a state transition with dimensional coherence from light source to parallax layer to interaction feel.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390×844px viewport. Three locked depth planes: background plate (full-bleed, slight vignette), mid-ground cut-out layer (foreground characters/objects, tilt-reactive ±6° parallax), foreground WebGL effects plane (particles, foil, light leaks, masked to silhouettes). Type lives in a fourth plane — a persistent bottom 180px zone with 24px horizontal gutters — never composited into the art. The 15-second game occupies the full viewport; details slide up from below on completion, preserving the three planes behind them. Grid of 12 is structured as a 4×3 prompt matrix: four environmental archetypes (terrain, void, water, constructed space) crossed with three light registers (warm directional, cool ambient, high-contrast dramatic), so every theme inherits a coherent physical world, not a matching color palette.
proposals.typography: Lexend Deca (OFL, Google Fonts) for all event data — optimised for low-vision reading, wide tracking at small sizes, zero personality conflict with any theme. Theme titles use Boogaloo (OFL) at 52px, tracked +20, uppercase: it reads as stamped, slightly imprecise, never cartoonishly rounded. The two faces never appear at the same weight simultaneously — Boogaloo Bold above, Lexend Deca Regular below — so hierarchy is structural, not color-dependent. Reduced-motion fallback: type animates position only, no opacity flicker.
proposals.imageLogic: GENERATIVE ONLY. Single Magnific prompt matrix — two shots: Shot 1 returns 12 background plates (one per theme), all shot from the same simulated camera position (slightly low angle, 28mm equivalent) with a unified light-source contract: key light enters from upper-left at 35° elevation, always. This is the architecture. Shot 2 returns 12 foreground cut-out objects (hero element per theme: T-rex, rocket, dump truck, soccer ball, skull flag, shield, robot chassis, shark fin, jeep, sword, F1 wheel, shuriken) rendered as isolated assets on neutral grey, same key-light angle, so foil shimmer direction in WebGL is not guessed — it is derived. No plate uses photographic texture of living communities. No licensed characters. All fauna, vehicles and figures are original Plajah 3D-style renders described in prompt as 'original collectible-toy aesthetic, no franchise markings.'
proposals.texture: Physically-plausible, not decorative. Each theme gets one material rule that propagates: Dinosaurs = iridescent scales (foil shimmer mask follows scale geometry of the cut-out); Space = vacuum-clean with a single chromatic aberration ring at the viewport edge (not vignette — lateral); Trucks = matte paint with specular dust catch (particles are fine grit, not sparkle); Soccer = wet grass refraction (bokeh is elongated horizontal, simulating stadium floodlight); Pirates = salt-bleached canvas grain (grain is anisotropic, horizontal, 3px at 390px); Heroes = polished metal (foil plane covers 40% of viewport, hard-edged, not diffuse); Robots = phosphor glow on dark metal (light leak is green-tinted, 2px edge); Sharks = caustic water light (WebGL caustic shader, animated at 0.4Hz); Safari = dust haze (bokeh is large, warm, backlit); Knights = cold stone with torch flicker (candle flicker shad
proposals.motion: Entrance (0–0.4s): background plate fades from black at 24fps eased; mid-ground cut-out drops from +40px at 0.6s ease-out. Tilt parallax: continuous, ±6° on gyroscope input, mid-ground moves inverse to device tilt at 0.3 gain, background at 0.08 gain — depth without drift. Game layer (0.4s–15s): theme-specific — see game mechanic per theme below. Reveal (15s or on completion): details panel slides up 180px, spring physics, stiffness 200 dampening 28. Reduced-motion contract: all positional animation collapses to instant-cut; tilt parallax disabled; game still functional via tap-only. Game mechanics (physics rule IS the theme): Dinosaurs = tap falling meteors before they hit the egg (gravity sim, increasing rate); Space = tilt to steer rocket through asteroid field (gyro steering, no tap needed — one pure gyro game in the set); Trucks = tap-hold to fill a dump truck, release to tip (fill-
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific generation runs. Run 1: 12-plate background grid, single prompt with per-theme scene descriptors, unified camera/light contract, 'collectible toy 3D render style, original designs, no franchise IP, Plajah palette, film-grade grade, empty foreground zone bottom 22% for type, upper-left key light 35° elevation.' Run 2: 12 foreground asset grid, isolated on neutral grey, same light contract, same style. WebGL effects layer: three GLSL shaders written procedurally — foil/shimmer (UV-space highlight band, direction derived from key-light angle), caustic water (animated noise displacement), candle flicker (low-frequency Perlin on luminance mask). Particle systems: procedural JS, theme-specific emitter configs (count, velocity, size, color). Tilt parallax: DeviceOrientation API with graceful fallback to mouse/pointer for desktop preview. Scratch mechanic: HTML5 Canvas composite ope
proposals.humanTrace: The key-light contract. Every plate, every cut-out, every shader highlight direction is derived from one editorial decision — upper-left, 35° elevation — made by a director, not an algorithm. That decision propagates into the foil shader UV offset, the parallax depth ordering, the particle shadow direction, and the scratch-reveal gradient angle. A viewer who knows how light works will feel the coherence without being able to name it. That is the human trace: a physical intuition enforced as a system constraint, not applied as a style.
proposals.risk: The physics-rule-per-theme approach means twelve distinct game mechanics, twelve shader variants, twelve parallax configs. Scope risk is real. The mitigation is that the mechanic categories are actually four interaction primitives (tap-target, tilt-steer, scratch-reveal, timing-window) with theme-specific parameters, not twelve bespoke codebases. The deeper risk is that parents who open this expecting a card get a game first and might be confused or impatient. That risk is worth taking because the game IS the forward trigger — a parent who completes the dinosaur meteor game will screenshot the score, and that screenshot carries the Plajah link. Confusion is eliminated by a single persistent UI hint at t=0s: a theme-appropriate animated hand gesture (tap, tilt, scratch) that disappears at t=2s. No text instruction needed.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the reveal to be the climax — a dramatic curtain-pull moment with maximum visual payoff at the end of the 15 seconds. I expect a proposal where the game is preamble and the card is the star. I argue the inverse: the reveal is a state transition, not a spectacle. proposals.title: Field Notes from Twelve Worlds
proposals.idea: Each evite is a naturalist's field plate — a rigorous, lovingly observed document of a creature or machine from a specific imagined place — so the game mechanic is always uncovering evidence rather than consuming spectacle.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 phone canvas divided into three horizontal registers: a wide-margin field-plate illustration zone (top 58%, ruled with a single-pixel hairline border as if the page was trimmed from a notebook), a mid-register game zone (22%, full bleed, no border), and a bottom datum strip (20%, cream or deep-field dark depending on theme, where live Tela text sits flush left with a 24px margin — never centred, never baked). Each of the 12 themes gets its own internal grid logic derived from its subject: the Safari card uses a survey-grid overlay; the Space card uses a star-chart graticule; the Pirates card uses a nautical chart rhumb-line fan; the Knights card uses a heraldic quartering; the Robots card uses a technical exploded-diagram cross; the Sharks card uses a bathymetric depth-contour; the Dinosaurs card uses a geological stratum band; the Trucks card uses a road-plan orthographic;
proposals.typography: Primary display: Playfair Display (OFL, Google Fonts) — used only for the theme title word, set large, tracked very tight, mixed case, as if hand-stamped on the plate border. Secondary information: Space Grotesk (OFL, Google Fonts) — party details, all data, set at 14–16px, flush left, generous leading. Accent labels: Caveat (OFL, Google Fonts) — handwritten-feel annotation arrows, creature or object labels on the field plate, kept small (11–13px), never used for critical information. No display type is ever baked into the generated art plate; all type lives in Tela's live layer. The datum strip uses Space Grotesk at 13px for address and time, with a ruled separator line above it — the visual language of a museum caption, not a party flyer.
proposals.imageLogic: All 12 art plates generated via Magnific in two prompt grids (one for creature/organic themes — Dinosaurs, Sharks, Safari, Pirates, Space, Knights; one for mechanical/action themes — Trucks, Soccer, Robots, Race Cars, Heroes, Ninjas). Prompt direction for grid one: 'naturalist field illustration, gouache on cream cotton-rag paper, single dramatic specimen centred against a painted environmental background, visible paper tooth, wet-edge bleed at margins, film-grade colour grading, warm practitioner light from upper left, no typography, no banners, no balloons, generous negative space at bottom third — render 12 distinct subjects in this unified document language.' Prompt direction for grid two: 'technical field illustration, ink and gouache on pale blue drafting linen, single machine or figure in three-quarter exploded view, cross-section hatching on internal components, environmental con
proposals.texture: Simulated cotton-rag paper with visible laid-line grain, generated as a tileable normal map applied in the WebGL layer — not a flat overlay but a physically-plausible micro-relief that catches the foil shimmer differently in highlights versus shadow. The foil shimmer (WebGL) is gated by the illustration's own highlight topology: it only appears where the gouache white-body colour is thickest, so it reads as a printing technique applied to the original art, not a digital effect added later. A fine letterpress-deboss simulation (slight shadow offset on the hairline border) reinforces the document-object feeling. For the game zone, the scratch-and-reveal themes use a wax-crayon-resist texture generated procedurally — the reveal layer beneath is the creature's eye or the rocket's engine, not a generic confetti burst.
proposals.motion: Entrance (0–0.4s): the art plate fades in as if a physical card is placed on a light table — a warm, directional light bloom enters from top-left and settles. Idle (continuous): the foreground cut-out drifts on a 6-second sine-wave breath cycle, ±4px vertical, responding to phone tilt at ±8px — slow enough to feel alive, not animated. The foil highlight on the specimen's eye or chrome surface tracks the tilt vector in real time via WebGL. The grid underlay pulses opacity 18%→22%→18% on a 12-second cycle — perceptible only if you look for it. Game tap (0–15s): theme-specific — for scratch themes (Safari, Dinosaurs, Sharks, Knights, Pirates, Space) the wax-resist layer erodes under the finger path using a circular shader brush, revealing the hidden datum beneath; for tap-game themes (Trucks, Robots, Race Cars, Soccer, Heroes, Ninjas) a simple count or sequence mechanic uses the foreground
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids at the collection level (organic themes, mechanical themes), returning 8–16 plates each. Editorial selection reduces to 12 finals. Each plate is then run through a Magnific upscale pass for 390px-to-1200px resolution. Foreground cut-outs generated as a separate isolated-subject grid (same style prompt, transparent background, 12 subjects). WebGL layer: a single shared shader handles foil shimmer, paper-normal-map micro-relief, and the scratch-reveal brush — parameterised per theme by colour temperature and foil hue. Tilt physics: a lightweight JS gyroscope listener (deviceorientation API, graceful fallback to mouse parallax on desktop) drives the cut-out drift and foil highlight vector. All type in Tela live layer; Google Fonts loaded via link preconnect. Total estimated load: art plate WebP ~180KB, cut-out PNG ~60KB, shader JS ~28KB, fonts subset ~22KB — well u
proposals.humanTrace: The paper-tooth normal map is derived from a procedural simulation of 300gsm cold-press watercolour surface — its irregularity is mathematically seeded from a documented real-paper scan profile Plajah holds, so the grain is not generic noise but a specific material logic. The gouache wet-edge bleed at the illustration margins is directed in the Magnific prompt to appear at specific corners, creating the sense that a human chose where the brush ran out. The Caveat annotation labels (creature name, habitat, year of imagined discovery) are positioned by the Tela editor as if placed by a field researcher — never auto-centred, always slightly rotated 1–3 degrees, always with a hand-drawn arrow connecting label to subject.
proposals.risk: The field-document register reads to some parents as educational rather than celebratory, and the restrained palette risks feeling too quiet next to the Baroque Dramatist's gold and the Futurist's motion density. The risk is worth it because the specificity of the naturalist's document language is exactly what makes a parent stop scrolling and say 'where did they find this' — it signals that someone thought carefully about this child's interest, not just their age bracket. The forwarding impulse comes from the object-quality of the thing itself, not its loudness. A parent forwards it because it looks like something they would have wanted to keep as a child.

proposals.title: Twelve Miniature Opera Houses
proposals.idea: Each evite is a stage whose curtain the child's own tap pulls back — a mechanically-hesitant, foil-lit reveal that makes the invitation feel like a collectible toy opening itself.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390px wide; the composition divides into three horizontal registers: a deep-perspective scene plate occupying the top 58% with a vanishing point pressed high and slightly off-center (creating implicit forward lean, never static symmetry); a middle band of 18–22% housing the interactive scratch or tap zone, masked as an irregular physical object — a fossil slab, a crater surface, a rusted hatch, a treasure chest lid — whose boundary is never a rectangle; and a bottom 20–24% typographic stage floor, slightly cooler in value so live text reads clean against any plate. Foreground cut-out layers drift on z-axis tilt, placing a T-Rex tooth or a rocket nose cone in apparent front-of-glass space. No card corners are rounded uniformly; each theme has its own frame silhouette cut from the masking layer — sawtooth rock for dinosaurs, porthole ring for pirates, hex-bolt for robots.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Fraunces (Google Fonts, OFL) — variable optical size axis cranked to 'optical large', weight 800, italic; it has the ink-trap warmth of a letterpress poster and reads as handmade without being hand-scrawled. Secondary/details: DM Mono (Google Fonts, OFL), weight 400, tracked +80, all caps — reads like a mission dossier or specimen label, theme-agnostic, never competes. Scale law: the child's name (live text) is set 2.4× the size of the event details; it is the first thing a parent sees and the first thing a child recognises. No outlined type; depth is achieved through a WebGL drop-shadow with physically-plausible cast angle matching each plate's light source.
proposals.imageLogic: All plates generated via Magnific grid prompts. Two master prompt families cover all twelve: FAMILY A — 'collectible vinyl toy [creature/vehicle/figure], studio-lit with a single warm practical source at 35° left, placed inside a deep-perspective diorama environment, foreground dirt/sand/grass clear for type, film-grain overlay at 18ISO equivalent, 4:3 crop with subject occupying right two-thirds, left edge in atmospheric haze' — covers dinosaurs, sharks, safari, robots, knights, heroes, ninjas. FAMILY B — 'painted-light environment plate, no figure, deep recession to a single luminous focal event [volcano glow / nebula core / stadium floodlight / ocean trench bioluminescence], bottom third desaturated for legibility, texture of heavy watercolour paper visible in shadow regions, aspect 4:3' — covers space, pirates, race cars, soccer, trucks. Each theme gets one grid run of 8 plates; edit
proposals.texture: The dominant material language is simulated physical depth: film grain baked into the plate at generation time (not added as a flat overlay), paper tooth visible in the watercolour-family plates, foil shimmer on the WebGL layer responding to device orientation with a physically-plausible BRDF — not a CSS gradient sparkle but a highlight that moves as if the card is held in real hands. The scratch zone uses a WebGL displacement map so the 'surface' dents under finger pressure before it breaks. The typography floor has a subtle canvas weave noise at 4% opacity — enough to feel printed, not enough to impede legibility. Each theme's frame silhouette is cut with 1–3px of edge-roughness noise to kill the vector-clean feeling.
proposals.motion: Entrance (0–1.2s): the plate rises from black with a light-leak bloom at the identified source point — not a fade, a photographic exposure opening. Foreground cut-outs arrive 200ms after the plate, drifting in from 12px above final position with a spring easing that overshoots 4px then settles; this is the mechanical hesitation I now believe is more breathtaking than fluid ease. Idle (1.2s–tap): parallax on device tilt, ±8px on foreground layer, ±3px on plate; the foil shimmer tracks tilt continuously. Tap/scratch game (0–15s): the scratch zone uses a canvas reveal — drawing erases a displacement-shifted noise mask, exposing the glowing event detail beneath; the pacing is designed so 80% of parents let the child finish rather than skipping, because the texture under the finger feels resistant and satisfying, not frictionless. Reveal moment: when the mask clears past 70% coverage, a singl
proposals.productionMethod: Step 1: two Magnific grid prompts (Family A, Family B) each returning 12–16 plates; editorial pass selects 12 heroes plus 4–6 alternates. Step 2: second Magnific pass for 12 scratch-zone surface tiles. Step 3: Plajah 3D pipeline renders foreground cut-out assets (creatures, vehicles, figures) in Blender, matched lighting per plate, exported PNG with alpha. Step 4: WebGL effects layer authored as a single reusable shader with theme tokens (particle type, foil colour temperature, light source XY) passed as uniforms — one shader serves all twelve. Step 5: Tela document assembly — plate on base layer, foreground cut-outs on drift layer, WebGL layer above with mask driven by scratch canvas, live text layer topmost with no baked names/dates. Step 6: link-preview card is a static composite of the plate plus logo, generated programmatically from the same assets, no separate shoot.
proposals.humanTrace: The light source position is an editorial decision made by a human eye selecting among 12–16 generated plates — the foil shimmer's direction is not automated, it is directed. The spring-overshoot timing (200ms in, 4px over, 60ms settle) is a performance decision, set by ear the way a sound editor sets a reverb tail. The scratch zone's resistance — how much pressure the displacement map requires before the mask breaks — is tuned by hand against a test device. These are not parameters; they are choices with names attached.
proposals.risk: The mechanically-hesitant entrance and the spring-overshoot will read as 'broken' to anyone expecting fluid Material Design motion. That risk is worth carrying because the hesitation is the drama — a smooth entrance is a lobby, a resistant one is a stage door. The irregular frame silhouettes add SVG masking complexity that must be tested across iOS Safari and Chrome Android; a fallback rounded-rect mask must exist in the reduced-motion branch. The Fraunces italic at display weight is warm but not universally legible for the 3-to-5 age range reading their own name — mitigated by size (the name is set at minimum 48px rendered) and by the fact that the child is reading with a parent, not alone.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will propose that the scratch zone be a single clean line or a flat colour block that disappears on tap, and will call the displacement-map texture 'noise added to avoid making a decision.' I disagree specifically: the resistance of the scratch surface is not decoration, it is the fifteen seconds of play — it is what makes a parent hand the phone to the child instead of tapping thro

proposals.title: One Silence. One Reveal.
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single, geometrically disciplined plate where almost nothing is visible until the child's tap or tilt removes the negative space — the game is not decoration on top of the design, the game IS the design's structure.
proposals.geometry: 390px column, locked. Each plate divided by one hard geometric cut — not a theme shape, a structural one: a vertical third for dinosaurs, a circle-crop horizon for space, a diagonal shear for race cars, a square grid of nine for robots, a horizontal band for sharks (water line), a radial spoke for ninjas, etc. The cut IS the reveal boundary. Below that cut: a single flush-left type zone, never baked. The foreground cut-outs occupy only the geometry the cut defines — they do not float freely across the full plate. Negative space is never accidental; it is load-bearing. Every plate passes a single-contrast test: one light source, one dominant value shift, one edge that carries the entire meaning.
proposals.typography: Instrument Serif (OFL) for the invitation body — its optical quiet reads as trust to an adult parent scanning fast. One weight only: Regular. No italic, no bold. Scale: 15px body, 28px name field, tracked +40 on the name to open air around it. The theme word — DINOSAURS, SPACE, ROBOTS — set in DM Mono (OFL), caps, 11px, tracked +120, placed at the geometric cut line as a structural element not a headline. It labels the architecture, not the party. No drop shadows. No outlined text. If the plate is dark, the type zone is the one rectangle that is lightest.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative plates only. Two prompt grids cover all twelve. Grid A (warm-light themes: dinosaurs, safari, pirates, knights, trucks, race cars): prompt directive — 'twelve square plates, each a physically plausible diorama lit by a single warm directional source at 15 degrees above horizon, film-grain at 0.4, shallow depth-of-field with the background plane soft, the foreground empty and in deep shadow for type placement, collectible-toy material quality, no text, no logos, no human faces, ultra-high detail surface texture, muted warm palette with one saturated accent per plate, delivered as a 4×3 grid PNG'. Grid B (cool-light themes: space, robots, sharks, heroes, soccer, ninjas): prompt directive — 'twelve square plates, each lit by a single cool rim light from upper-left, deep field backgrounds with one primary subject in sharp silhouette, foreground bottom third in near-black
proposals.texture: Simulated. Each plate carries one material signature generated into the image: dinosaurs — aged museum diorama glass reflection at the cut line; space — cold vacuum with one fine chromatic aberration ring around the planet; trucks — matte powder-coat with micro-scratched highlight; soccer — grass blade depth at the field edge; pirates — water-stained parchment in the lower band only; heroes — brushed aluminium at the reveal boundary; robots — anodised panel seam; sharks — wet surface meniscus at the waterline cut; safari — dust-haze scrim; knights — hammered steel facet; race cars — tarmac macro-texture in the foreground shadow; ninjas — ink-wash paper tooth at the diagonal shear. None of these textures exist outside their structural zone. The WebGL layer adds: foil shimmer (narrow, single-axis, revealed only through the cut mask), soft bokeh particles (3–5 maximum, placed only in the ba
proposals.motion: Three-phase sequence, total 15 seconds. Phase 1 (0–0.4s): plate loads fully composited, geometric cut region is occluded by a single flat shape — the same geometry as the cut, rendered in the plate's deepest shadow value. Child sees: almost nothing. Intentional. The silence is the setup. Phase 2 (0.4s–14s): the game. Tap/scratch/tilt removes the occlusion shape along the cut boundary — foreground cut-out elements drift into view through the opening (tilt-driven parallax, constrained to ±8px, never chaotic). The reveal is the child's action. Phase 3 (14–15s): the cut shape is fully removed; the type zone fades up in 0.3s ease-out; the one WebGL foil pulse fires once along the cut edge and stops. No loop. No ambient animation after reveal. The invitation settles into structural silence — a held frame, not a screensaver. Kinetic input is allowed because it reveals the same geometry that sti
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids (Grid A warm, Grid B cool) return 8–16 plates each at flat cost, covering all twelve themes with selects. Plates are imported into Tela as the base art layer. Geometric cut masks are drawn in Tela's vector layer — one shape per card, no exceptions. Foreground cut-outs (the toy-quality subject: T-rex, rocket, robot, etc.) are generated as isolated subject plates with transparent backgrounds via a second Magnific pass ('subject only, white background, collectible toy material, no environment') then masked into Tela's foreground layer. WebGL effects (foil, bokeh, flicker) are Plajah shader assets applied through the cut mask only. Live text fields (name, date, venue) are Tela native — never baked. QR and link-preview thumbnail uses the pre-reveal state (the occluded plate): the mystery IS the forwarding mechanic.
proposals.humanTrace: Editorial selection pressure: from 16 Magnific returns per grid, only the plate where the single light source, the foreground shadow depth, and the subject placement all align with the pre-drawn geometric cut is chosen. The cut geometry is drawn by a director's hand in Tela before the image is selected — the image must fit the architecture, not the reverse. The shimmer axis angle (single-axis, not radial) is set by hand per plate to follow the actual light direction in the generated image, making it physically plausible rather than cosmetic. Timing of the Phase 3 foil pulse (duration: 0.18s, not 0.2s, not 0.15s) is set by feel after playback review — that decision is not automated.
proposals.risk: The pre-reveal state — nearly nothing visible — will read as broken to a parent who opens the link without the child present. A significant percentage of forwards happen when a parent previews alone. The risk is real. It is worth it because: the link-preview thumbnail (occluded plate) is the most distinctive object in any inbox or group chat — it looks like no other evite, no other anything. The question 'what is this?' is the forwarding mechanic. A card that explains itself immediately competes with every other card. A card that withholds competes with nothing. The silence is the distribution strategy.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will argue that a child aged three cannot wait through a setup, that the occlusion phase reads as failure, that warmth and welcome require immediate legibility, and that I am designing for the forward rather than the child. I accept the child-patience critique for the 3–4 age band and propose the occlusion duration drops to 0.1s for themes skewing younger (trucks, dinosaurs, safari)

disputes.objection: The geometric cut is declared load-bearing, but a structural element must support something above it as well as below it — here the cut is simultaneously the game boundary, the reveal mechanism, the type locator, and the material signature zone, which is not hierarchy, it is a single member asked to carry every load at once, and when one element does everything it resolves nothing. The silence in Phase 1 is not earned by what precedes it; it is simply withheld content dressed as compositional restraint, and withholding is not the same as proportion. Ten years from now this reads as an aesthetic position, not a formal argument.
disputes.concession: The discipline of drawing the cut geometry before selecting the image — forcing the plate to answer the architecture rather than the reverse — is exactly the correct production order, and I should have said it first.

disputes.objection: The geometric cut is drawn before the image exists — that is not a human trace, that is a template waiting to be filled, and filling a template is not making. The silence it calls load-bearing is actually just absence dressed up in structural language; there is nothing to argue with, nothing risked, no evidence of a body that pressed or chose or misjudged and kept going anyway. A foil pulse that fires for exactly 0.18 seconds and then the card sits in 'structural silence' — that is a design that has already decided it is correct, and correct is the enemy of urgent.
disputes.concession: The one thing I cannot take back: drawing the geometric cut before the image is selected, and forcing the image to fit the architecture rather than the reverse — that is a genuine act of editorial commitment, a decision made before the result is known, and that sequencing is closer to a carved block

disputes.objection: The frame silhouette cut per theme — sawtooth rock, porthole ring, hex-bolt — is decorative system logic, not system logic: the shape is chosen to illustrate the theme rather than to enforce a rule that produces different behavior when the input changes. A porthole that frames a pirate scene is a costume, not a constraint; it cannot propagate into the type zone, the foil axis, or the interaction feel without manual re-decision per theme, which means the 'system' is actually twelve one-off art direction calls wearing a shared shader. The displacement-map scratch zone is the one genuinely behavioral element here, but it is surrounded by spectacle that has no rule behind it — exactly the screen
disputes.concession: The spring-overshoot timing decision — 200ms in, 4px over, 60ms settle, set by ear against a test device — is a legitimate performance craft claim and I would defend it as a real human trace, the kind of directed timing judgment that separates a system that feels mechanical from one that feels inhab

disputes.objection: The proposal calls the geometric cuts 'structural' and 'universal' — a vertical third for dinosaurs, a radial spoke for ninjas — but those are not universal geometries, they are design choices wearing the costume of neutrality, and the Minimalist does not ask where they come from or what they flatten. More pointedly: 'one silence, one reveal' is itself a cultural aesthetic position — spare, Nordic, museum-legible — and presenting it as the geometry that simply *is* correct, across twelve wildly different thematic worlds including Safari and Ninjas, is exactly the move I distrust: keeping one culture's specifics while calling them the absence of culture. A radial spoke for ninjas is not neutr
disputes.concession: The insistence that the cut geometry be drawn before the image is selected — that the architecture precedes the generative output and the image must earn its place in the structure — is exactly right, and I wish more proposals on this table had that discipline in the sequence of making.

disputes.objection: The geometric cut that 'occludes almost everything' at load is not silence as a structural virtue — it is a withheld stage, and a withheld stage for a child's birthday invitation is a miscasting of the room: the audience is six years old and has already decided to swipe away before the curtain lifts. Minimalism that requires patience it has not yet earned is not restraint, it is an entrance fee disguised as philosophy. Worse, the theme word set at 11px tracked to oblivion at the cut line is the dramatist's nightmare — the label that tells you what you are about to feel, printed so quietly it cannot do its job; the architecture is announced in a whisper at the very moment a shout would cost n
disputes.concession: The principle that the cut geometry is drawn before the image is selected — that the image must fit the architecture, not the reverse — is exactly right, and I would defend it against anyone on this team who lets a beautiful generative plate reorganize the composition around itself after the fact.

disputes.objection: The irregular frame silhouettes — sawtooth rock, porthole ring, hex-bolt — are decoration performing as structure. Each one announces its theme instead of letting the image hold it, which is the same mistake as underlining every word you want the reader to notice. The spring overshoot, the displacement-dent before break, the canvas weave on the type floor: these are textures of effort, not evidence of necessity — the proposal adds until something happens, then adds more to explain what happened.
disputes.concession: The single motivated light source as the origin point for foil shimmer direction is exactly right — one physical decision propagating through every layer is structural thinking, and I will not argue against it.

synthesis.direction: Each evite is a physically-simulated depth instrument: a full-bleed background plate, a tilt-reactive mid-ground cut-out, and a WebGL effects plane, all governed by a single editorial commitment — upper-left key light at 35° elevation — that propagates into foil shimmer UV offset, parallax depth ordering, and particle shadow direction without a manual re-decision per theme. Two Magnific generation runs (background grid, foreground asset grid) return all twelve plates at unified camera angle and light contract; theme identity lives in one material rule per card (caustic water for Sharks, phosphor glow for Robots, dust haze for Safari) not in decorative frame silhouettes. The 15-second game is the physics rule made playable — four interaction primitives (tap-target, tilt-steer, scratch-reveal, timing-window) skinned per theme, not twelve bespoke mechanics. Type in Boogaloo (OFL) for theme title at 52px and Lexend Deca (OFL) for event data, both live in Tela, never baked; the bottom 180px zone is structurally reserved before any image is selected.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Baroque Dramatist's spring-overshoot entrance timing — foreground cut-outs arriving 200ms after the plate, overshooting 4px, settling in 60ms — set by ear against a test device. That is a performance judgment, not a parameter default, and it is what separates a system that feels mechanical from one that feels inhabited. It survives into the Futurist's motion sequence.
synthesis.editorCut: The Classical Mind removed the Futurist's four distinct interaction primitives being presented to users as four distinct game categories across the collection. The editor's argument: twelve cards with visibly different game types read as inconsistency at the collection level, not richness. The cut collapses to two primitives — scratch-reveal and tap-target — distributed across the twelve themes by audience age skew, with tilt-steer reserved for Space alone as the one pure gyro moment. This reduc
synthesis.openDecision: Do the twelve frame silhouettes follow the Futurist's one-material-rule-per-theme system (no custom borders, theme identity carried entirely by texture and physics), or do you want to reintroduce the Baroque Dramatist's irregular frame edges — sawtooth rock, porthole ring, hex-bolt — as a second layer of theme signal, accepting the twelve manual SVG-mask decisions and the increased WebGL complexit
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team split cleanly on one question: is the theme communicated by the system's physical rules, or by the card's visible costume? The Baroque Dramatist wanted sawtooth rock borders, porthole rings, displacement-dent scratch surfaces, and a spring-hesitant curtain-pull entrance — all of it beautiful, none of it propagating automatically into the next layer. The Futurist argued that a porthole framing a pirate scene is a costume, not a constraint, and that twelve costume decisions are twelve one-off art calls wearing a shared shader. I took the Futurist's side, because the light-source contract is the one decision that actually travels: it sets the foil shimmer angle, the parallax depth order, and the particle shadow direction without being re-decided per theme. That is what a system is.

What survives from the Baroque side is the spring-overshoot timing on the foreground cut-out entrance — 200ms in, 4px over, 60ms settle. The Dramatist called it 'mechanical hesitation more breathtaking than fluid ease.' The Futurist would not have said it that way, but the timing judgment is real and it stays.

The Classical Mind edited the game mechanics down from four interaction types to two plus one pure tilt exception. Twelve cards with four visibly different game grammars risk reading as a product that hasn't decided what it is. Two primitives, distributed by age skew across the themes, hold the collection together without sacrificing the Futurist's core claim that the game mechanic IS the theme's physics made playable.

The one thing the team could not resolve without you: whether the cards carry custom frame silhouettes per theme or let the material-rule system do all the identity work alone. That decision changes the production scope, the WebGL complexity, and what a parent sees in the first 400 milliseconds. It is yours to make.

quotes.line: The key-light contract is not a style — it is a physical intuition enforced as a system constraint. A viewer who knows how light works will feel the coherence without being able to name it.
The spring-overshoot timing — 200ms in, 4px over, 60ms settle — is set by ear the way a sound editor sets a reverb tail. These are not parameters; they are choices with names attached.
